note: Implementation choices and approval gates, not delivery status. Local recommendations may guide synthetic work; approvals are absent until an accountable person signs the exact scope. No vendor is purchased or enabled here.

choices.title: Operating scope and legal coverage
choices.recommendation: India-only service. Synthetic local development uses declared fictional tasks. First live legal pack is the reviewed Telangana/Union task list, not all Indian law.
choices.rationale: User-confirmed India-only scope; source holdings are not verified capability.
choices.fallback: Do not enable another jurisdiction, language or practice task without a separate reviewed pack.
choices.approver: product owner and qualified Indian counsel

choices.title: Local architecture and data authority
choices.recommendation: Keep Python/FastAPI/current browser UI. PostgreSQL 18, current supported minor, owns new private transactional state; encrypted object storage owns media; existing public-law SQLite/FTS adapters remain until measured replacement.
choices.rationale: Minimises rewrite risk and gives one authoritative write path. No new graph service or Redis authority.
choices.fallback: Use isolated encrypted filesystem/object fixtures for synthetic contracts only; this does not satisfy cloud KMS or production store proof.

choices.title: Hosting residency and service boundary
choices.recommendation: Preferred procurement shortlist: AWS Mumbai primary and Hyderabad recovery for regional application/database/object/key services. Verify each exact service, support and telemetry path and quote before selection. No public CDN caching of protected material.
choices.rationale: Official regional availability makes this a concrete starting shortlist, not proof that every processor or service confines all data to India.
choices.fallback: Until service-specific region/contract approval, use local synthetic services with external egress disabled.

choices.title: Authentication and recovery assurance
choices.recommendation: Retain current invitation and identity store contracts for local work. Confidential profile uses a maintained identity component/provider bridge with user-verifying WebAuthn/passkey or approved MFA and controlled factor recovery. Never implement cryptographic verification ad hoc.
choices.rationale: Avoids replacing proven identity attribution while making strong authentication an early prerequisite.
choices.fallback: Local scripted factor fixtures test orchestration only. Existing explicit login-error policy remains on controlled local endpoints; neutral confidential-profile errors require recorded adoption.

choices.title: Models transcription and document processors
choices.recommendation: Keep provider adapters. Use deterministic/scripted responses for local tests; choose live processors only after India processing/retention/no-training terms and required capability benchmarks are demonstrated. For the selected operation/configuration, prohibit automated biometric identification or voiceprints, affect/emotion scoring and voice/appearance credibility inference, including unavoidable background processing. Verify absence before procurement/adoption and before transmission, with runtime drift checks. Optional unrelated vendor services do not themselves disqualify a permitted transcription operation. No automatic foreign fallback.
choices.rationale: A provider brand or region label alone is not a confidentiality or quality approval.
choices.fallback: Keep affected voice/OCR/model capability disabled or manual-source-assisted until a compliant processor is approved.

choices.title: Capacity latency and cost budgets
choices.recommendation: Reference engineering load:25 named synthetic accounts,20 sessions,5 reasoning tasks,2 ingestion jobs. Use the documented proposed SLOs; require priced per-task and monthly INR budgets before costly runs or pilot provisioning.
choices.rationale: Makes workload reproducible without inventing vendor prices or claiming measurements.
choices.fallback: No paid model batch or load test without a bounded run approval; cheap local tests remain permitted.

choices.title: Legal sources review and evaluation rights
choices.recommendation: Preserve the shared legal corpus; classify source rights and identity before publication. Qualified reviewers approve legal premises, treatment labels and hidden-test answers. Synthetic protocols are not legal gold labels.
choices.rationale: The corpus audit was bounded, and public availability alone does not establish redistribution rights.
choices.fallback: Discovery-only or unsupported states until source and legal-use review is complete.
choices.approver: qualified Indian counsel and data owner

choices.title: Retention restoration and incident operation
choices.recommendation: Use purpose-specific reviewed retention and hold rules with tombstones. Proposed pilot disaster design target: RPO <=15 minutes and RTO <=4 hours, subject to priced rehearsal and client-facing approval. Durable acknowledged writes have no permitted loss during ordinary process restart.
choices.rationale: Separates ordinary durability from disaster recovery and funds operational commitments before promises.
choices.fallback: Synthetic restore/tabletop only until the named operator, legal applicability, budget, contacts and achieved recovery results are approved.

choices.title: External action scope
choices.recommendation: First release prepares, verifies and exports approved drafts; the advocate files/sends and records receipts. Automated send/file/settle connectors are disabled until separate scoped approval and unknown-outcome reconciliation proof.
choices.rationale: Delivers useful action support without inventing authority or reliable external delivery.
choices.fallback: Manual verified receipt capture; never simulate a filed or sent status.

choices.title: Release accountability and adoption
choices.recommendation: Only a named release manifest and accountable sign-off can admit a confidential pilot or production. Adoption records name the exact design, implementation, source/model/provider versions and unresolved limits.
choices.rationale: Planning integrity and executed legal/security evidence are distinct claims.
choices.fallback: Keep scope synthetic-only and the release claim closed until approvals and actual proof are present.
choices.approver: product owner, engineering, security/privacy and qualified counsel reviewers
